subject: Request: SLA credit adjudication + telemetry bundle for Oct 12 availability blip
messages:
From: Rajesh Kaur <rajesh@finhive.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: FinHive Platform Ops <ops@finhive.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Service disruption window and SLA relief request

Hi Grace,

We observed an elevated error rate and request timeouts for the FinHive checkout path between 14:02 and 14:18 PT on Oct 12. Our SRE team flagged ~6% failed checkouts vs baseline and dozens of retries. This impacted the final mile and caused a measurable revenue impact for our peak window.

Can Redwood confirm the observed service window on your side, and advise whether this meets the SLO exception conditions in our contract? If eligible, we’d like to start the credit adjudication process. We have attached a CSV of our frontend error metrics; happy to share additional telemetry.

Immediate ask: please confirm the Redwood-observed incident window and the next steps to request a proration/credit.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Rajesh Kaur
Director, Platform Engineering
FinHive Inc

Attachments: finhive_metrics_20261012.csv (CSV)

From: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Kaur <rajesh@finhive.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service disruption window and SLA relief request

Rajesh,

Thanks for the heads up and for the CSV — I can see how painful this would be during checkout. We have preliminary telemetry that shows an uptick in 500/502 responses routed to the "checkout" model group around 14:03-14:16 PT.

To expedite adjudication we need:
- A short statement of impact (est. revenue or transaction count affected).
- Your frontend and network traces (if you can share) and the exact timestamps you used to compute the 14:02-14:18 window.

I’m looping in Marcus (support) and Diego (infra) to grab the raw traces and to confirm the Redwood-side consolidated window. Expect a trace bundle from us by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will produce a raw trace bundle + token-level latency histogram and a suggested prorated credit calculation.
2) We will triage for root cause; if Redwood is found responsible under the SLA, we will propose the credit.
3) If the root cause is external, we will provide the evidence and next steps for joint remediation.

I’ll follow up with the bundle.

Best,
Grace Oconnor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Service disruption window and SLA relief request

Grace / Diego,

Forwarding FinHive request. I pulled the candidate traces from the checkout model group for 14:00-14:20 PT and ran a quick token-latency aggregation. Preliminary notes:
- Error spike (500/502) aligns with our autoscaler throttling loop during a temporary control-plane hiccup.
- Impacted requests: ~2.2k requests, average additional latency +420ms for affected tokens.

I attached the trace bundle and a short CSV extract that maps our request ids to their error codes. Diego, can you confirm whether there was a config rollout in that region or if any node preemption occurred around that time? Evelyn, feel free to add legal/finance for the credit calculation owners.

Attachments: redwood_trace_bundle_20261012.zip

Marcus Lin
Customer Support Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Kaur <rajesh@finhive.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service disruption window and SLA relief request

Hi all,

We completed the log reconciliation and agree on the consolidated impact window of 2026-10-12T14:03:08-2026-10-16T14:15:42 PT (14:03-14:15 local window). Our telemetry shows an autoscaler control-plane stall due to an ephemeral scheduler deadlock; there was a transient preemption event in one node pool that momentarily reduced available workers.

Credit proposal (initial):
- We propose a pro-rata credit for the affected 12-minute window using the standard formula in section 4.2 of the contract (monthly usage * impacted_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_period).
- Based on FinHive's submitted usage for Oct and our measured affected request volume, preliminary credit = $6,120. We will finalize after cross-checking your attachable transaction list.

Next steps:
1) Grace to confirm acceptance of the preliminary window and the calculation methodology.
2) FinHive to send a short impact statement and the transaction ids for reconciliation (we can handle a sampling approach if that is helpful).
3) Finance to open a credit memo (Evelyn, can you start the draft and mark as pending until reconciliation completes?).

Rajesh, I’ll leave the detailed trace bundle in the shared Drive folder and I’ve also attached a mutual action plan PDF with timeline for remediation and follow-ups.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan_2026-10-13.pdf
